title: Balance concurrency, latency, and cost
summary: Choose capacity changes using representative workload evidence.
objectives: Choose capacity changes using representative workload evidence.
Apply capacity tradeoff to the worked customer example and explain its limits.

questions.prompt: The median improves, but 10% of queries still exceed 60 seconds. Is a 95%-under-15-seconds objective met?

options.text: No; the tail exceeds the allowed failure proportion.
options.rationale: A median does not establish the required percentile objective.

options.text: Yes, because the average user is faster.
options.rationale: The agreed criterion is not the median.

options.text: Yes, if the new warehouse is more expensive.
options.rationale: Price is not evidence of meeting the latency threshold.

options.text: To remove all difficult queries from the comparison.
options.rationale: That changes the workload rather than testing the configuration.

options.text: To prove all serverless and classic settings behave identically.
options.rationale: The documented models differ and need their own context.

options.text: To see whether peak-oriented capacity creates avoidable off-peak consumption.
options.rationale: The operating cost spans more than the best-performing peak run.

cards.prompt: How do latency and throughput differ?
cards.answer: Latency is time to a result; throughput is completed work per time.
cards.explanation: Capacity planning needs both under a defined concurrent workload.

cards.prompt: What is the key limit of an hourly compute price comparison?
cards.answer: It omits how much resource is consumed and other relevant costs.
cards.explanation: Compare a consistent workload and total cost basis.

cards.prompt: Why avoid promising proportional speedup from more resources?
cards.answer: The bottleneck and parallelism may limit or change the effect.
cards.explanation: Measure the representative workload instead of extrapolating a resource label.

cards.prompt: A dashboard is slow only at 08:00 each morning. Which delay component do you separate first?
cards.answer: Compute startup and queueing under the peak population, measured apart from execution and rendering time.
cards.explanation: A warehouse that must start, or that queues twelve simultaneous refreshes, adds waiting that a quiet-hour test never shows. Record queue time, startup state and concurrency beside execution time, then test one capacity or scheduling change against the same workload and success rule.
